verdict.content_summary: This describes a skill for the Hermes agent that was not authored but accumulated: whenever Hermes worked out a procedure or corrected a mistake during repo work, it saved the lesson into a Markdown skill document (with optional reference files/scripts) that it loads on later tasks. The agent itself writes and revises these docs, making the skill a living, self-maintained knowledge base derived from its own operating history. The content surfaces two concrete techniques captured this way: a clean-environment repro on unchanged origin/main HEAD to classify a failing test as pre-existing vs. introduced, and a frozen-baseline comparison used during a multi-worker refactor to separate baseline-inherent failures from integration-introduced ones.

grabs.what: Self-accumulating agent skills: the agent appends reusable lessons to a Markdown doc as it works, instead of skills being written upfront
grabs.why: Directly portable to their local AI agents. Their stack is markdown-first and their coding/document agents already produce structured output; adding a rule like 'when you fix a mistake or discover a working procedure, append a dated lesson to skills/<topic>.md' turns their repos into agent memory with zero new infrastructure — no cloud, no new account, SQLite-simple.

grabs.what: Clean-HEAD baseline repro rule: run a failing test on unchanged code in a clean environment before debugging
grabs.why: This is a drop-in verification step for any agent pipeline that touches their repos — it stops agents from 'fixing' pre-existing breakage and polluting diffs. Worth baking into their coding-agent prompts or skill files verbatim, since it's a one-line procedure with high signal.

grabs.what: Frozen-baseline diffing for parallel integration: check failures from worker output against a frozen reference to isolate newly introduced errors
grabs.why: Maps cleanly onto their multi-model routing through OpenRouter: when several small models work in parallel on one codebase or document set, comparing each worker's failures against a frozen baseline separates model-introduced regressions from pre-existing noise — the same triage problem they'll hit the moment they fan work out to multiple models.

aspects: Agent-authored procedural memory: the system writes and revises its own instruction docs from operating history, so knowledge compounds instead of being spec'd upfront
Skills as loadable Markdown plus scripts: machine-readable-but-human-editable knowledge the agent reads at task time, no proprietary format
Baseline classification: distinguishing pre-existing failures from introduced ones by reproducing on a clean reference point before acting
Frozen-reference integration: evaluating parallel/merged work against a fixed snapshot so inherent noise doesn't mask regressions
adjacency_queries: LLM agents that persist lessons learned into markdown memory files during autonomous work, rather than fixed system prompts
CI tooling that runs failing tests on a clean baseline commit to classify pre-existing versus newly introduced failures
merge queue or integration bots that diff errors against a frozen baseline when combining work from parallel contributors
open-source formats for agent skill files that pair markdown instructions with executable scripts a local agent loads at runtime

finds.name: SAKU (omohikane/saku)
finds.what_it_is: Self-evolving local AI agent (Python, MIT) with persistent personality and Markdown memory, running on small local models (llama-cpp, Ollama, Qwen) and journaling into Obsidian-compatible notes.
finds.different_angle: Shares the core mechanism of the triaged content — an agent accumulating its own knowledge base from operating history instead of a fixed prompt — but applies it to a personal companion/journaling domain rather than repo-work skills, and grounds the loop in local models instead of a cloud agent.
finds.why_relevant_to_profile: Matches the profile's local-model, self-hosted, offline-first stack and markdown-first notes; the journal-to-memory growth loop is a portable pattern for the profile's own agents' lesson accumulation.

finds.name: Regression triage & baseline diff (koreaelonmusk/entropy-loop-core)
finds.what_it_is: Docs describing a deterministic, fully local baseline-diff: compare two JSON test reports and classify each case as newly failing, fixed, already failing, or missing, emitting a JSON or Markdown report.
finds.different_angle: Takes the triaged content's frozen-baseline comparison out of the agent's learned heuristic and makes it an explicit deterministic tool — classification by report diff rather than by re-running on a clean origin/main HEAD.
finds.why_relevant_to_profile: Pure structured in/out (JSON reports in, classified JSON/Markdown out), runs locally with no service; the classify-movement logic can be ported directly into the profile's ingest pipeline or CI scripts.

finds.name: claude-code-merge-queue (funador)
finds.what_it_is: Local, zero-cost merge queue (MIT, npm) that serializes landing, building, and testing for parallel Claude Code agents working in git worktrees.
finds.different_angle: Attacks the same multi-worker integration problem as the frozen-baseline technique, but prevents integration failures by serializing landings against latest main instead of diagnosing them after the fact.
finds.why_relevant_to_profile: The profile runs multiple local agents on self-hosted infrastructure; this is cheap, single-purpose, composes with git worktrees, and needs no SaaS queue.

finds.name: quietclash (arbade/quietclash)
finds.what_it_is: Small MIT tool that detects silent behavioral conflicts between parallel coding agents — branches that merge cleanly and pass tests but break at runtime.
finds.different_angle: Extends the frozen-baseline comparison from test results to runtime behavior: it catches integration-introduced breakage that the triaged content's test-based baseline diff would miss entirely.
finds.why_relevant_to_profile: Directly useful when the profile's parallel local agents touch the same codebase; small, self-hostable, and the behavioral-diff idea ports into the profile's own pipelines.

finds.name: AgentSkills Spec (choutos/agent-skills-spec)
finds.what_it_is: Open, framework-agnostic MIT specification for packaging procedural knowledge as SKILL.md files — markdown instructions plus optional scripts — that agents load at runtime.
finds.different_angle: Formalizes the triaged content's skill-file format (markdown doc + reference scripts) as a portable inter-agent standard, rather than one agent's self-accumulated convention.
finds.why_relevant_to_profile: The profile wants open formats and mechanisms to port; this spec lets its own agents write and read interchangeable skill docs without locking into any vendor's framework.
